fields.meta_title: Customer Feedback Survey That Sorts Comments | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a customer feedback survey that sorts comments by theme, saves each answer with its customer and routes complaints to an owner.
fields.h1: Build a Customer Feedback Survey and Act on Every Comment
fields.hero_description: Describe who you want to hear from and what you need to learn. Emergent builds the survey, along with the app that stores and acts on what customers say.
fields.features_heading: What a Feedback Survey Has to Do
fields.features_subheading: Each part of a customer feedback survey below moves a comment one step closer to being fixed.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written from your goal

Each question ties back to the one thing you need to learn, in plain words. Customers see one question per screen and can answer each one on a phone with a single thumb.
fields.feature_2:
Sends tied to real events

Start the survey when an order is delivered or a free trial ends in your billing tool. Any tool with an API can trigger a send, and each send is logged against the customer.
fields.feature_3:
Comments sorted by type and theme

Tag every open answer by type, such as a bug or a complaint, then group it by theme with a count. A product lead reads 15 themes instead of scrolling through 400 comments.
fields.feature_4:
Context saved with each answer

Store the customer ID and plan with every response, plus the order, store or technician involved. Filter by any of them to see where one complaint keeps coming from.
fields.feature_5:
Complaints sent to one owner

Route a low rating, or a comment that mentions a refund, to the person who can fix it. The Slack message or email quotes the comment in full, with no login to read it.
fields.feature_6:
Code and answers you can take with you

Answers live in a database you own. Export the survey and its sorting rules to your GitHub repository whenever you like, together with every answer collected so far.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Places to Ask for Feedback
fields.tab_content_1:
Find out why subscribers cancel

Once Stripe reports a canceled subscription, the subscriber gets a three-question email: the main reason, what would bring them back and anything else. Each answer is saved with the plan and months subscribed. Over 30 days, 112 of 160 canceling subscribers answered, and price led with 41.
fields.tab_content_2:
In-app comments, sorted before anyone reads them

A feedback button sits on every screen of your web app. Each comment is saved with the page and the account's plan, then tagged as a bug, idea, question or praise. When one bug is reported 9 times in a week, the product team's Slack channel gets the count and the comments.
fields.tab_content_3:
A text after every repair visit

Two hours after the technician closes the job, the customer gets a text through Twilio. It asks for a star rating, whether the tech arrived in the booked window and what went wrong, if anything. A rating of 2 or lower becomes a callback task for the dispatcher, with the job number and the comment.
fields.tab_content_4:
Which store slipped this week, and why

Shoppers at all 12 stores scan a QR code printed on the receipt and answer four questions on their phone. Answers roll up by store each week. When a store's score falls more than 0.5 points, its district manager gets an email with the drop and the most common complaint.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Customer Feedback Survey
fields.howto_description: Settle these seven calls before the first survey goes out. Emergent builds the survey around whatever you decide.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick one decision the answers should settle, such as whether to extend support hours or which onboarding step to rewrite. A survey without one collects opinions nobody owns. Put that decision at the top of your prompt.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Set the delay for each moment. A haircut can be rated the same evening, while a delivered blender needs a week of use first. Ask about one moment per survey instead of the whole relationship.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Use one rating and one open question, with the open question right after the rating, where it asks why. Ask about one thing per question: rating the food and the price together gives a number nobody can read.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Run the survey open-ended with a small group first. Recurring answers become the choices in your reason list. At a gym, members who leave might keep naming class times or parking. The open box stays for everything the list misses.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the survey to your own phone from a test account, then watch what happens. Check that it arrives and the answer lands in the table. Then rate it 1 and confirm the alert reaches its owner.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Decide what is worth an alert
fields.howto_step_6_des: A customer who says they are leaving needs a reply today. Ten mild notes about font size can wait for the weekly read. Set a threshold for each owner, high enough that every alert still gets read.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the comments before the scores
fields.howto_step_7_des: A rating says something went wrong, and the comment says what. Each week, read the comments behind the lowest ratings before opening any chart. Then tell customers what changed because they answered, in the channel the survey came through.

plan.angle: The top 10 is question lists, glossary definitions and survey-tool landing pages (easy-feedback, QuickTapSurvey, LimeSurvey). None shows what happens to the open-text answers. This page answers the PAA questions (how to write one, the three C's, how to analyze feedback, the types of feedback) and then shows four feedback surveys whose comments get read and routed: a cancellation survey fed by Stripe, an in-app feedback button sorted by type, a text after a technician's visit, and a QR survey across 12 retail stores. scope.evidence: H1 "Build a Customer Feedback Survey and Act on Every Comment"; hero "Emergent builds the survey, along with the app that stores and acts on what customers say." Whole job, not the customer-satisfaction sibling's score focus.

intent.evidence: All five on-topic PAA questions answered; sample questions in FAQ 3; template question in FAQ 8; seven-step how-to; meta promises (sorts by theme, saves with customer, routes complaints) delivered in features 3-5.

specificity.evidence: Stripe cancellation event, Twilio text two hours after a repair, receipt QR across 12 stores, 0.5-point drop to the district manager; survey-builder table rows.

openers.evidence: features_subheading "Each part of a customer feedback survey below moves a comment one step closer to being fixed."; howto_description "Settle these seven calls before the first survey goes out." Both full sentences.

craft.evidence: Steps no longer retell the tabs: step 1 "whether to extend support hours or which onboarding step to rewrite", step 4 gym members naming class times or parking, step 6 "Ten mild notes about font size can wait".

voice.evidence: Plain verbs and unglamorous detail ("a delivered blender needs a week of use first", "Missed our window."); no AI tells.

truth.evidence: FAQ 7 no longer defines CES ("If you also track a customer effort score, keep it in the same app"); McKinsey three C's, Pew wording/order and double-barreled, SurveyMonkey no fixed count, Stripe and Twilio match domain_sources; free-start and no-caps in the ledger; 41+33+21+17 = 112.

distinct.evidence: Angle is comments and action, not the live customer-satisfaction page's score; QC Q6/D2 clean.

faq.evidence: 10 items, each answered in sentence one ("There is no fixed five.", "Lists vary, and there is no fixed count.", "Yes."); FAQ 7 now adds "did the problem stay fixed?", FAQ 8 names post-onboarding and delivery surveys.

images.evidence: 112 of 160, price 41; 9 bug reports to #product-feedback; job #4471 at 2 stars to the dispatcher; Store 07 down 0.7 emailed to the district manager. One hero per tab; numbers add up.
